provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Microbial exopolysaccharides (EPS) produced by bacteria and fungi as bio-adsorbents for heavy metals and dyes. Rich in functional groups for pollutant binding.

mechanisms.description: EPS functional group binding: carboxyl, hydroxyl, and sulfate groups on exopolysaccharides coordinate heavy metal ions and cationic dyes

pollutant_feature.value: Heavy metal ions and cationic dyes

mechanism.value: Coordination with carboxyl, hydroxyl, sulfate groups on EPS

performance_expectation.value: EPS can bind significant amounts of heavy metals

engineering_constraints.description: EPS production: microbial fermentation, yield depends on species and conditions

narrative.text: Microbial exopolysaccharides are natural biopolymers secreted by bacteria and fungi. They contain abundant functional groups (carboxyl, hydroxyl, sulfate) that can bind heavy metals and dyes. Production is scalable via fermentation.

design_translation.idea: Produce exopolysaccharides via microbial fermentation and use as bio-adsorbents for heavy metals and dyes
examples: Xanthan gum for heavy metal adsorption
design_translation.applicability: Heavy metal and dye removal from wastewater

knowledge_gaps: Need primary research papers with quantitative performance data
